extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers; infectious disease epidemiologists, geospatial analysts, and mathematical modelers working on HIV-TB
extracted.subtask_description: Research strategy section of an R01 proposing geospatial and transmission modeling to evaluate district-level HIV-TB dynamics and preventive therapy strategies in Uganda, including stakeholder engagement and cost-effectiveness analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geospatial modeling approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Geospatial models using a small area estimation approach appropriate for rare disease outcomes in geographic districts (polygons) will be developed for HIV-TB prevalence, incidence and mortality using a Bayesian statistical approach with template model builder (TMB) in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draws strength from neighboring regions in time and space to stabilize estimates for rare outcomes. Includes data at different geographic resolutions (regional survey and district notifications) to generate district-level estimates. Report uncertainty bounds by generating 1000 candidate maps from the posterior distributions of model parameters and report the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population-weighted aggregation of within-district predictors
rubrics_metrics.description: For predictor data that varies across the district, such as population density, undernutrition and poverty rate, the population-weighted mean value for the district will represent the entire district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use population-weighted calculations (GIS) to aggregate gridded or facility-level maps to district-level summaries to reduce bias from spatial heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health facility accessibility and diagnostic capacity measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a model of district-level accessibility to health facilities with the clinical and laboratory capacity to diagnose TB using maps of health facilities, road networks, and poverty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map facility locations, road networks, and poverty to create an aggregate measure of accessibility. Include presence of smear microscopy and/or Xpert MTB/RIF equipment as indicators of diagnostic capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictor selection for multivariate models
rubrics_metrics.description: Predictors with a significant bivariate relationship with each outcome will be included in multivariate models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen predictors via bivariate analyses before inclusion; use established statistical selection rules to avoid overfitting given rare outcomes and small-area estimation context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome data sourcing and triangulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes: TB mortality among PLHIV from Ministry of Health DHIS-2 by district (2012-2017); HIV-TB prevalence primarily from the 2014-2015 national TB prevalence survey; HIV-TB incidence estimated from TB case notifications adjusted for underreporting using treatment seeking maps and diagnostic capacity. Incidence will also be triangulated from district-level prevalence and mortality using the transmission model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin in 2012 because TB mortality was first included in DHIS-2 that year. Use population-based survey data to better ascertain cases than surveillance alone. Adjust notifications for underreporting using modeled treatment-seeking behavior and diagnostic capacity; triangulate using transmission model outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling frame and statistical power
rubrics_metrics.description: The sample size of 112 districts yields >90% power to detect a modest correlation (>0.3) between the predictor and outcome variables assuming a slope of 0.10 in a linear regression model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power calculation performed with Sampsi_reg, Stata v14. Report assumptions and detectable effect sizes for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: District-level deterministic transmission model structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt a deterministic compartmental model of HIV-TB co-infection with compartments for TB-uninfected, latent TB infection (with or without preventive therapy), active TB, and recovered; each TB compartment subdivided by HIV and ART status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same model structure for each district but allow district-specific parameter values informed by geospatial model outputs. Numerically solve differential equations in R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameterization and calibration strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Fit district-specific parameters for disease progression using a maximum likelihood approach, inputting prevalence and mortality estimates (from Aim 1) and literature-derived parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use half the districts (N=56) for calibration and reserve the remaining 56 for validation. Compare parameter values between calibration and validation runs and against published models. Use literature and surveillance data (detailed in Table 2) to inform priors/ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: External and internal validation of model
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate the transmission model predictions using data from an additional year of surveillance (2018) not used for calibration, and by reserving half the districts for out-of-sample validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use validation comparisons to assess key mechanistic drivers and validate district-level estimates. Report discrepancies and use them to refine model assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for cross-district care-seeking
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate travel for care-seeking, recognizing patients may seek care outside their home district; model Kampala with surrounding districts if data indicate substantial cross-district care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use surveillance data that include home district of patients to assess and model spatial patterns in care-seeking and adjust notification-based incidence estimates accordingly. Compare household prevalence survey data with case notifications to localize missing patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: ART effect on TB progression
rubrics_metrics.description: In the model, ART reduces the risk of progression from latent TB infection to active TB by 65%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this parameter (65% reduction) based on cited literature; incorporate ART coverage trends (2006-2016) due to time-lag in HIV disease progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic review methodology for PT effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete a systematic review of the impact of preventive therapy (PT) on TB incidence, mortality, drug resistance, and severe adverse events following Cochrane Collaboration guidelines and PRISMA reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop search strategy with a research librarian; include PubMed, Embase, and conference abstracts. Stratify studies by PT regimen (6-9 months isoniazid vs 1-3 months weekly rifapentine+isoniazid) and ART use; assess covariates such as TST/IGRA positivity, CD4 count, diagnostic method, and PT duration. If heterogeneity prevents meta-analysis, use bounds from study assessments to parameterize models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for multidrug-resistant TB
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate multidrug resistance into the model by varying PT efficacy parameters to reflect possible reductions in preventive therapy effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although MDR prevalence in Uganda is low (~1.6%) and prior meta-analyses suggest no significant increase in resistance after IPT, vary efficacy parameters in sensitivity analyses similar to prior modeling work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model outcomes and DALY calculation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Model outcomes include incident TB cases among PLHIV, TB-associated mortality, and DALYs averted by PT. DALYs will be calculated with a 0% discount rate and without age-weighting to conform with current Global Burden of Disease Study methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report results on multiple time horizons (1, 5, 10, 15 years) and present uncertainty bounds for each outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy-relevant scenario definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare scenarios: (1) uniform distribution of PT across all health facilities providing ART versus (2) prioritization of PT to facilities and community ART programs in regions with greatest TB prevalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate that geographic prioritization will have greater health impact; identify regions where PT risks may outweigh benefits. Use model to quantify trade-offs to inform decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costing approach and micro-costing data use
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate incremental costs of delivering PT and treatment costs incurred/averted using micro-costing data from existing studies and NTLP budget reports for drug costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use micro-costing for community-based and clinic-based PT implementation cost estimates; conduct sensitivity analyses for key cost parameters and estimate cost efficiencies of uniform vs regional strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness analysis criteria and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) per incident HIV-TB case, death, and DALY averted. Interventions considered cost-effective if ICER <3× local GDP per DALY and very cost-effective if ICER <1× GDP per DALY, per WHO guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Panel on Cost-Effectiveness in Health and Medicine guidelines; report ICERs and costs for 1-, 5-, 10-, and 15-year timeframes; present sensitivity analyses across key parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized evaluation of stakeholder engagement format
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomize stakeholders to receive model results in an interactive versus passive format to quantify differences in implementation outcomes (acceptability, feasibility, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervention arm: brief presentation followed by hands-on interaction with model visualizations on a tablet. Control arm: presentation with opportunity to ask questions. Randomization implemented via algorithm in R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of implementation outcomes framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt Proctor et al.'s framework of implementation outcomes (acceptability, feasibility, adoption, fidelity, cost, penetration, sustainability, appropriateness) to assess stakeholder perceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a questionnaire targeting acceptability and feasibility (suitable for pre-intervention assessment). Use these constructs to structure analysis and reporting of stakeholder responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: User interface and data visualization standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an interactive user interface allowing stakeholders to alter model inputs and receive predictions in multiple data visualization formats; maps and charts will be available and users can focus on region or whole-country model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage IHME visualization approaches; support a dedicated programmer with grant funds. Visualizations should facilitate stakeholder understanding and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder recruitment and eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit ~30 senior program leaders from NTLP, TB Union, CDC Uganda, and UAC (roles: Program Manager, Project Team Lead, District Health Officer). Participants must be adults (≥18) and fluent in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use introductions from research group and affiliated public health officials; target senior decision-makers likely to influence policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionnaire design and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured questionnaires administered in private locations and in English by a study investigator; questionnaires focus on model inputs, barriers to implementation, familiarity with modeling, prior use of modeling for decisions, and perceptions of acceptability and feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use primarily numerical responses (e.g., Likert scales). After sessions, administer an approximately 15-minute tablet-based questionnaire. Use questionnaire comments to inform modeling (without formal qualitative analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder data analysis plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Report responses to stakeholder questionnaires by theme based on implementation outcomes; calculate descriptive statistics using R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use descriptive statistics for numerical items and thematic grouping for comments. Comments inform modeling contextually but are not subjected to formal qualitative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit acknowledgement of limitations and alternative approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that TB under-detection, differences in transmission dynamics across settings, limited LTBI data, and potential delays in external data (e.g., IHME model) may limit analyses; propose alternative data sources and sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize triangulation (prevalence, mortality, transmission model) when notifications are imperfect; vary key parameters across plausible ranges; prepare contingency plans for delayed external datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and permissions for external data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a combination of publicly available data (DHS, WorldPop, TB prevalence survey) and collaborators' data (NTLP, DHIS-2, IHME) with permissions documented via letters of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document data provenance and permissions. When external geospatial products (e.g., IHME HIV prevalence maps) are delayed, identify alternative district-level HIV prevalence sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter sourcing and citation for model inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive transmission model parameter values from national surveillance (NTLP), the literature, and epidemiologic data (summarized in Table 2 with cited sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each parameter with its source and justification; where uncertainty exists, use ranges informed by literature and incorporate into sensitivity analyses.
